title: Riesling
description: Germany's great grape: piercing acidity, pure fruit and every sweetness level, from bone dry to luscious.
L: Riesling gives whites with lime, lemon, green apple, peach, apricot and white flowers, with a mineral, sometimes smoky edge. Acidity is very high. It's almost never oaked or put through malolactic, so its fruit is pure and transparent. It ranges from bone dry to intensely sweet, and from light to full-bodied.

Riesling comes from the Rhine valley in Germany, first recorded in 1435 near Rüsselsheim. DNA shows one parent is Gouais Blanc; the other was a Traminer crossed with a wild vine. It buds late and ripens late, so it needs a long season. Its hard wood resists winter cold well, ideal for northern vineyards.
Why is Riesling's fruit so pure and transparent?
It's rarely oaked or put through malolactic
Without oak or malolactic, nothing masks its fruit or place.

Look for pale lemon, sometimes green-tinged colour, intense lime, apple and flower aromas, and very high acidity. Sweet versions balance sugar with that acidity. Aged Riesling shows honey, toast and a petrol note. High acidity with floral, citrus fruit and no oak is the signature.
Not true. It buds and ripens late, needing a long season.
Riesling gives lime, peach and flowers with very high acidity
It comes from the Rhine, recorded in 1435
It's rarely oaked, so it shows fruit and place clearly

Germany grows about 40% of the world's Riesling, in the Mosel, Rheingau, Pfalz, Nahe and Rheinhessen. Alsace makes dry, fuller Riesling. Austria's Wachau, Kamptal and Kremstal make dry, powerful versions on steep terraces. It's also grown in northern Italy and across central Europe.

Australia's Clare and Eden Valleys make dry, lime-scented Riesling that ages toward toast. New Zealand's Marlborough and Central Otago, Washington State, New York's Finger Lakes and Canada's Niagara also excel. Riesling needs cool or moderate climates to keep its acidity and aromas.
Match each region to its Riesling style.
Each region gives Riesling a different accent.

Because Riesling is unoaked and unblended, it shows soil and site clearly. Slate gives smoky, delicate wines; volcanic soils give spice; limestone gives tension; loess gives roundness. That's why Germany and Alsace name single vineyards on labels, like Burgundy.
What share of the world's Riesling does Germany grow?
Germany is by far the largest producer.
Germany grows about 40% of the world's Riesling
Australia, Austria, Alsace and North America also excel
Riesling shows soil and site with unusual clarity

Germany's top quality level, Prädikatswein, is graded by the sugar in the grapes at harvest, measured in degrees Oechsle. The six levels: Kabinett, Spätlese, late harvest; Auslese, selected bunches; Beerenauslese, selected berries; Eiswein, frozen grapes; and Trockenbeerenauslese, dried, botrytised berries. Minimums vary by region.

A Prädikat says how ripe the grapes were, not how sweet the wine is. A Spätlese can be fermented dry, labelled trocken, or left off-dry or sweet. Trocken means up to 9 g/l of sugar; halbtrocken up to 18 g/l; feinherb is an unofficial off-dry term. Beerenauslese, Eiswein and Trockenbeerenauslese are always sweet.
Order these Prädikat levels from least to most ripe.
Each level demands riper grapes; TBA requires shrivelled, botrytised berries.

Germany's VDP, an association of top estates, uses its own vineyard classification: Gutswein, Ortswein, Erste Lage and Grosse Lage. Its top dry wines are labelled Grosses Gewächs, GG, from Grosse Lage sites. Many VDP members use Prädikat terms only for sweeter wines.
What does trocken on a German label mean?
Dry, up to 9 g/l of sugar
Prädikat levels grade ripeness at harvest, from Kabinett to TBA
They show ripeness, not necessarily sweetness
The VDP's GG means dry wine from a top site
Explain the balance of sugar and acidity

Dry Riesling, from Alsace, Austria, Australia and Germany's trocken and GG wines, is crisp and mineral, with citrus and stone fruit. Off-dry Riesling, like many Mosel Kabinetts, balances a little sugar with high acidity, often at only 7.5 to 9% alcohol, tasting fresh rather than sweet.

The balance between sugar and acidity defines Riesling. High acidity, often 8 to 10 g/l, makes even 40 or 50 g/l of sugar taste only slightly sweet. The International Riesling Foundation created a taste profile scale, from dry to sweet, that some producers print on the back label to help buyers.
Why does an off-dry Mosel Kabinett taste fresh rather than sweet?
Acidity counters the perception of sweetness.

Auslese, Beerenauslese, Eiswein and Trockenbeerenauslese are sweet, sometimes extremely so: TBA can exceed 300 g/l of sugar, with only 6 to 8% alcohol. Riesling's acidity keeps them lively. These are among the longest-lived wines in the world.
Which Riesling styles are usually dry?
TBA is among the sweetest wines in the world.
Riesling ranges from bone dry to intensely sweet
High acidity balances sugar, making off-dry wines taste fresh
Sweet Riesling can exceed 300 g/l and live for decades

Aged Riesling often smells of petrol, kerosene or rubber. The compound is TDN, 1,1,6-trimethyl-1,2-dihydronaphthalene. It forms from carotenoids in the grape skins, more so with strong sunlight, heat, drought and low yields. Australian Riesling, under intense sun, often shows it early. Some love it; others find it a flaw in excess.

Young Riesling shows fresh lime, apple and flowers. With 5 to 10 years, it gains honey, toast, beeswax and dried apricot, and colour deepens to gold. High acidity preserves it: good dry Riesling ages 15 to 20 years; sweet Auslese and TBA can age 50 years or more.
What favours the formation of TDN in Riesling?
Sun exposure increases carotenoids, which become TDN.
If you dislike strong petrol notes, look for Riesling from cooler sites, like the Mosel. Hotter, sunnier regions tend to show more TDN.
Good sweet Riesling can age for 50 years or more.
Yes. Sugar and high acidity preserve it.
TDN gives aged Riesling its petrol note, more with sun
With age, Riesling gains honey, toast and beeswax
Dry Riesling ages 15 to 20 years; sweet styles 50 or more

Dry Riesling suits fish, shellfish, pork, sushi and Alsace's choucroute. Off-dry Riesling suits spicy Asian food: Thai, Sichuan, Indian; its sugar and low alcohol calm chilli. Sweet Riesling suits fruit desserts, blue cheese and foie gras. Riesling's acidity cuts fat and salt.

Serve Riesling at 7 to 10 degrees; aged and sweet styles a little warmer, 10 to 12. Use a white wine glass with a narrowing rim to focus the aromas. Riesling under screw cap ages well and avoids cork taint.
Why does off-dry Riesling suit spicy food?
Its sugar and low alcohol calm chilli heat
Sweetness soothes, and low alcohol doesn't amplify the burn.
Mosel Kabinett with a spicy Thai salad is one of the great wine and food matches. The wine's lime and sweetness echo the dish.
Dry Riesling suits fish, pork and choucroute
Off-dry Riesling is a top match for spicy food
Serve at 7 to 10 degrees in a narrowing glass
Order the Prädikat levels from least to most ripe.

Why does Riesling age so well?
